questions.question: If someone is driving aggressively behind you, what should you do?

options.text: Move out of the aggressive driver's way.
Stare at the driver as they pass you.
Speed up while they are passing you.
Block the passing lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move out of the aggressive driver's way.
questions.explanation: Get out of the way of an aggressive driver. Do not make eye contact with them. Do not speed up, as this may make them angrier and more dangerous.

questions.question: If a police officer stops you, what should you do?

options.text: Unbuckle your seat belt and lower your window.
Get your paperwork ready before the officer reaches your car.
Stay in your vehicle with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer.
Get out of your car and walk toward the patrol car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your vehicle with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer.
questions.explanation: Keep your hands on the wheel and tell passengers to keep their hands visible. Stay in your vehicle unless the officer asks you to get out. Wait for the officer to ask for your driver's license, registration, and insurance card.

questions.question: When driving on an interstate, you must change lanes safely when approaching:

options.text: A stopped police vehicle with flashing blue lights.
A stopped emergency vehicle with flashing red lights.
A stopped maintenance vehicle with flashing amber lights.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must change lanes to give more space to stopped police vehicles with blue lights, emergency vehicles with red lights, and maintenance vehicles with amber lights. If you cannot safely change lanes, slow down instead.

questions.question: What can distract a driver?

options.text: CD players, iPods, cell phones, and GPS devices.
Food and drinks.
Pets moving around in the vehicle.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Using any portable electronic device while driving is illegal. Do not eat or drink while driving. Keep pets in carriers while the vehicle is moving.

questions.question: What does a green arrow on a lane control signal mean?

options.text: You may use this lane.
No traffic is allowed in this lane.
You have the right-of-way.
You must merge into this lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may use this lane.
questions.explanation: A green arrow pointing down over a lane means you can use that lane.

questions.question: How can you help reduce road rage and aggressive driving?

options.text: Allow extra travel time.
Obey posted speed limits.
Use proper turn signals.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: To prevent road rage, use your turn signals, follow the speed limit, and leave yourself plenty of travel time.

questions.question: When you hear a fire engine siren behind you, what must you do?

options.text: Slow down until it passes you.
Drive with your flashers on.
Pull over to the side of the road and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear an emergency vehicle siren, pull over to the curb or side of the road and stop.

questions.question: You hear a siren behind you while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Stop where you are.
Pull over to the right and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an emergency vehicle behind you, safely pull over to the right side of the road and stop. If you are in heavy traffic, move slowly until you can get out of the way.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on an interstate highway, what should you do?

options.text: Stop and make a U-turn.
Get off at the next exit and return to the exit you missed.
Roll down your window and ask the driver next to you for help.
Back up on the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get off at the next exit and return to the exit you missed.
questions.explanation: Do not back up or turn around on the highway if you miss your exit. Go to the next exit and turn around safely.

questions.question: What should you do when an emergency vehicle approaches with flashing red or blue lights?

options.text: Try to reach your destination before the emergency vehicle catches up.
Keep driving but try to stay out of its way.
Pull over to the side of the road and stop completely.
Stop in the middle of an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the side of the road and stop completely.
questions.explanation: You must yield to all emergency vehicles using sirens and flashing red, blue, or white lights. Pull over to the right edge of the road when possible. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first before pulling over.

questions.question: When a police officer is directing traffic at a working traffic light, drivers should:

options.text: Follow what the traffic light shows.
Follow the officer's directions.
Honk at the officer.
Watch what other cars are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the officer's directions.
questions.explanation: When a police officer is directing traffic, always follow their directions instead of the traffic light. Officers direct traffic to prevent crashes and keep traffic moving smoothly.

questions.question: What is the only way to lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?

options.text: Drink coffee.
Exercise.
Wait for your body to process the alcohol.
Take a cold shower.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for your body to process the alcohol.
questions.explanation: Only time lowers your BAC. Coffee, exercise, and cold showers cannot reduce your BAC or make you sober. They may keep you awake, but they do not lower your BAC.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on the interstate, you should:

options.text: Cut quickly across traffic to make your turn.
Make a U-turn to go back.
Keep driving and take the next exit.
Put your car in reverse to go back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep driving and take the next exit.
questions.explanation: Never make a sudden turn to catch a missed exit. If you pass your exit, continue to the next one.

questions.question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, you must:

options.text: Follow the crossing guard's directions.
Do what other cars are doing, even if it goes against the guard's directions.
Assume the guard should not be there.
Follow normal rules as if children were not present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the crossing guard's directions.
questions.explanation: Always follow directions from crossing guards and police officers in school zones. Slow down and be extra careful when you see signs, guards, or officers telling you to do so.

questions.question: What should you do when you see this sign?

options.text: Look for a train station ahead.
Signal before going further.
Slow down and let trains pass.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let trains pass.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a railroad crossing is ahead. Slow down when you approach railroad tracks. Trains cannot stop for cars, so you must always yield to trains.

questions.question: Smoking or getting ready to smoke while driving:

options.text: Does not affect driving.
Helps you stay alert.
Is a distraction.
Is not a distraction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is a distraction.
questions.explanation: Smoking while driving is dangerous. It takes your hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road, creating a distraction.

questions.question: On a long trip, a good way to stay awake is to:

options.text: Stop and rest every two hours.
Do arm exercises every hour.
Drive with one eye closed.
Switch which foot you use on the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest every two hours.
questions.explanation: Take a short break every two hours on long trips to prevent tiredness. If you feel drowsy, pull over safely and take a nap or find a place to sleep for the night.

questions.question: A driver taking an over-the-counter medication should:

options.text: Read the label before driving.
Drink alcohol instead.
Drive anyway, even if there are warnings.
Only drive during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Read the label before driving.
questions.explanation: Many over-the-counter medicines can affect your driving. Check the label for warnings before driving. Ask your doctor or pharmacist if you are unsure about how medication affects your ability to drive.

questions.question: Which of these statements is true?

options.text: You must use headlights from 30 minutes after sunset to 30 minutes before sunrise.
Using low beam headlights during the day can reduce head-on collisions.
You must turn on headlights when snow, rain, or fog reduces visibility.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Use headlights from 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise. Use low beam headlights at all times, even during the day, to help other drivers see you. Always use headlights when weather reduces visibility.

questions.question: If a tire blows out while you are driving, you should:

options.text: Brake hard immediately.
Keep the wheel straight and slow down gradually by releasing the gas pedal.
Keep the same speed and steer straight.
Swerve back and forth to warn cars behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the wheel straight and slow down gradually by releasing the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: If a tire blows out, grip the steering wheel tightly and keep the car straight. Release the gas pedal slowly. Once the car is under control, brake gently and pull over to a safe spot.
